tasks.title: Version the intervention record to intervention/v2: the schema, reading v1 and v2, writing v2, the derived agreement
tasks.goal: Every later task stands on this record: it adds schemas/intervention.v2.json, teaches the parser the v2 frontmatter (options, recommended, decided, adjusted, agreement) and the Context, Options, Recommended, Suggested and Decided sections, and makes add write v2. It also fixes the blind spot the brief exists for: 66 v1 records hold Context, Suggested and Decided sections that today's parser folds into done. The agreement is derived from the option count, the decided choice and adjusted, never stored on trust or read from prose, so a record that disagrees with itself is invalid.

references.why: the JSON form intervention/v2 extends: v2 is exactly v1's fields plus options, recommended, decided, context, suggested and agreement; nothing of v1 is renamed or dropped
the intervention's id and on-disk shape the record keeps, and C-3: every JSON document carries schema <name>/v<n> and unknown keys stay allowed

acceptance: schemas/intervention.v2.json is embedded and listed by `vloop schema list` beside intervention/v1: v1's JSON form plus `options` (an array of at most three strings), `recommended` ({option, why}), `decided` ({option, adjusted, text}, option 0 for other or none), `context`, `suggested` and `agreement` (one of recommended, other-option, adjusted, different, no-options).

A v2 record's frontmatter is v1's plus, in this order right after `by:`, `schema: intervention/v2`, `options: <0-3>`, `recommended: <0-3>`, `decided: <1|2|3|other|"">`, `adjusted: true` (only when adjusted) and `agreement: <…>`; the body is the summary, then **Trigger.**, **Done.**, **Context.**, **Options.** (a numbered list 1. to 3., one line each), **Recommended.**, **Suggested.**, **Decided.**, **What would automate it.**, each only when it has content.

A record without `schema: intervention/v2` reads as v1 with agreement no-options, and its **Context.**, **Suggested.** and **Decided.** sections parse into context, suggested and decided.text; done holds only the **Done.** section.

agreement is derived in one place from the option count, decided and adjusted, exactly by the brief's I1 table; a record whose stored agreement, `options` count or numbered list disagree, or that has options and `decided: ""`, makes `vloop intervention list` exit 1 naming the file. Violation to rule against: an agreement computed from the decision's text, or a stored agreement trusted without re-deriving it.
`vloop intervention add` with only v1's flags writes an intervention/v2 record with options 0, recommended 0, decided "" and agreement no-options; the v1 flags are unchanged.

Committed tests the checks run: TestAddWritesRecord pins the v2 bytes; TestExistingRecordsParse reads v1 and v2 records, including a v1 record's Context, Suggested and Decided sections; new unit tests cover every row of the derivation table and each kind of invalid record; the schema lists in internal/cli/schema_test.go, cmd/vloop/b2_e2e_test.go (TestWorkedExampleB2Commands) and internal/schema/schema_test.go gain intervention/v2.

TestListOrderFilterAndRoundTrip's assertion that a freshly added record's schema is intervention/v1 changes to intervention/v2, as a direct consequence of add writing v2; no other existing test is weakened or deleted.

tasks.title: Record options with vloop intervention add: --context, --option, --recommended, --why, --decided-option, --decided-other, --adjusted, --decided
tasks.goal: This is how the operator skill records what the model proposed and what the operator decided, so the evidence for which decisions a driver could take over starts accumulating. Up to three real options are recorded as given, never padded; the recorder says which option was chosen, adjusted or that something else was, and vloop derives the agreement (T1's derivation). Every malformed combination is refused before anything is written, with the brief's exact message.
acceptance: `vloop intervention add` accepts `--context '<paragraph>'`, `--option '<sentence>'` (repeatable, at most three), `--recommended <n>`, `--why '<reason>'`, `--decided-option <n>`, `--decided-other`, `--adjusted` and `--decided '<sentence>'`, and writes options, recommended, decided, adjusted and the derived agreement in the frontmatter and the texts in the Context, Options, Recommended and Decided sections.

Each refusal exits 2, writes nothing and prints exactly one stderr line, word for word as the brief's I2 quotes it: `vloop: at most three options`, `vloop: options need --recommended and --why`, `vloop: --recommended must name an option, 1 to <n>`, `vloop: options need --decided-option or --decided-other`, `vloop: --decided-option must name an option, 1 to <n>`, `vloop: --decided-option and --decided-other exclude each other`, `vloop: --adjusted needs --decided-option`, `vloop: --recommended, --decided-option and --decided-other need options`.
One or two options are recorded as one or two; nothing pads to three.
Without options the record is no-options and every v1 flag works unchanged.
`vloop intervention list`'s text output gains the agreement as a column, and TestInterventionAddListSet pins the new format.
Committed tests in internal/cli/intervention_test.go (or beside it) cover each refusal's message, exit code and that nothing was written, and each agreement add can produce.

tasks.title: Correct a record with vloop intervention set: recommended, decided and adjusted, re-deriving agreement
tasks.goal: The operator corrects a record by setting the choice, never the agreement: that keeps agreement tied to the options. `set` gains recommended, decided and adjusted, validates each against the record's option count, and re-derives agreement in the same write; agreement and options themselves stay unsettable, with the brief's messages.
acceptance: `vloop intervention set <id> recommended|decided|adjusted <value>` accepts recommended 1 to the option count, decided 1 to the option count, `other` or `""`, and adjusted `true` or `false`; a value outside the record's option count (including any decided on a record without options) is refused, the file untouched.
Every accepted set rewrites agreement in the same write, by T1's derivation; the body of the record is not changed; `adjusted: true` appears only while the decided option is adjusted.

`set … agreement …` exits 2 with exactly `vloop: agreement is derived — set decided, adjusted or recommended instead`; `set … options …` exits 2 with exactly `vloop: options are recorded with the intervention, not set`; neither touches the file. Violation to rule against: any path that writes agreement from a value the caller supplied.
The v1 fields (brief, phase, kind, automatable, by, occurred) stay settable as before.
Committed tests cover each new field, the re-derived agreement after each set, and both refusals.

tasks.title: Add vloop intervention migrate: v1 records to intervention/v2, frontmatter only
tasks.goal: The existing records move to v2 by the operator's explicit act, not silently: migrate inserts the five no-options lines after by: and changes nothing else, so the history the records hold is untouched and their options are never reconstructed. T10 runs it on this repository's own records.
acceptance: `vloop intervention migrate` rewrites every v1 record under .vloop/interventions/ by inserting `schema: intervention/v2`, `options: 0`, `recommended: 0`, `decided: ""` and `agreement: no-options` right after `by:`, and changes no other byte of the file; `recorded` and `backfilled` are left as they are. Violation to rule against: a migration that re-renders the record, normalises whitespace, or touches the body.
It prints `migrated <n> record(s)`, or `nothing to migrate` when no record is v1, and is idempotent; v2 records are left byte for byte.
`--dry-run` lists the files it would migrate and writes nothing.
`vloop upgrade` neither calls migrate nor rewrites any record.
Committed tests cover the byte-for-byte insertion, the dry run, idempotence, and that upgrade leaves a v1 record alone.

tasks.title: Add vloop intervention show <id>, resolving the ids written in its Context
tasks.goal: A record's context names the run, task, commit, defects and other interventions it concerns; show prints the record and resolves those ids so a reader need not chase them. Only the Context section is scanned, so a link is something the recorder chose to name; no new reference fields are added.
acceptance: `vloop intervention show <id>` prints the id and summary, the frontmatter fields, then each section under its name, then `links` with one line per id found in the Context section only, in order of first appearance.

A defect id D<…> resolves to its summary; an intervention id I<…> to its summary; T<n> to the task's title in .vloop/state/state.json of the latest `[vloop] plan <run id>` commit for the record's brief; a 7-to-40-hex word git resolves to a commit to its subject; a run id B<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>-<slug> to its run folders under .vloop/state/runs/. An id that resolves to nothing prints `<ref>  (not found)`.
`--json` prints the record's JSON form plus `links: [{ref, kind, title}]`.
An unknown id exits 1 with `vloop: no intervention <id>` on stderr, and under --json prints `{"error": …}` on stdout as `vloop task show` does.
Committed tests cover each kind of link, not-found, the order, the JSON form and the unknown id.

tasks.title: Report agreement across briefs: vloop metrics --interventions, by kind and by phase, and across a workspace
tasks.goal: This is the table that answers what a driver could take over: kind by agreement beside automatable, over every record including series-level ones, computed from the records themselves. Phase is the second cut, and the workspace form pools several repositories.

references.why: M-1: metrics are recomputed from raw sources — the table is counted from the records each time, never stored
the by-kind and automatable analysis done by hand that this table must reproduce from the records

acceptance: `vloop metrics --interventions` prints a header `kind  n  recommended  share  other-option  adjusted  different  no-options  automatable-yes  automatable-partly`, one row per kind in intervention/v1's kind order, then a `total` row, over every record in the repository including series-level ones.
share is recommended ÷ (n − no-options) as a whole percentage, `n/a` when n − no-options is 0.
`--by phase` prints the same table by phase in phase order (first column phase); `--by kind` is the default; `--json` prints the rows.
`vloop metrics --workspace <file> --interventions` prints the same table over every repository the file lists, with a `repo` column first, then a total row over all of them.
`--by task` with `--interventions` exits 2 with exactly `vloop: --by takes kind or phase with --interventions`.
Committed tests cover the counts, share including n/a, both orders, the workspace table and the refusal.

tasks.title: Add the interventions line and object to per-brief metrics and the close snapshot, and agreement and options to the export
tasks.goal: Per brief, the summary and its JSON (and the snapshot written at close) gain the interventions count by agreement, so a brief's record shows how often the model's recommendation was taken. The export gains the agreement and the option count per intervention but never the options' text, the reason, the decision or the context. Both are additive keys on existing schemas, not new versions, and every other number stays as it was.

references.why: gains an optional interventions object {total, by_agreement}; it stays metrics/v2 and nothing in it becomes required
the intervention record gains optional agreement and options (the count); it stays export/v1
M-7: an export carries numbers and titles only — so never an option's text, the reason, the decision or the context; C-3: additive keys, unknown keys allowed

acceptance: `vloop metrics <brief>` prints, on the line right after `defects`, `interventions  <n> · recommended <a> · other-option <b> · adjusted <c> · different <d> · no-options <e>`, counting the brief's records only; series-level records (brief "") belong to no brief.

Its JSON, and the snapshot `vloop brief close` writes, gain `interventions: {total, by_agreement: {…the five agreements…}}`; metrics/v2 declares it as optional; every other key of a brief's metrics is unchanged.

Each intervention line of `vloop metrics export` gains `agreement` and `options` (the count) and still validates as export/v1. Violation to rule against: an option's text, the reason, the decision or the context anywhere in the export.

Committed tests: the metrics and snapshot tests that pin the per-brief summary gain the interventions line; internal/cli/export_test.go TestExportInterventions gains agreement and options among the keys and asserts none of the four texts is exported.

tasks.title: Teach the operator skills to propose options and record them, and add the operate-proposes-options eval case
tasks.goal: The record is only as good as what is put in it: whenever the operator skill brings the operator a decision, it now proposes up to three real options, recommends one and says why, and records the intervention with those flags after the operator decides. The eval case is the skill's gate, run by the operator later; it must exist and be gradeable now.

references.why: the shipped playbook that gains the options rule and the recording flags; its existing steps and voice stay
this repository's playbook; only step 6 (recording interventions) and the index refresh change, to follow the shipped rule

acceptance: plugin/skills/operate/SKILL.md says that whenever it brings the operator a decision it proposes up to three real options, never a straw option to reach three, recommends one and says why, and after the operator decides records the intervention with `--option`, `--recommended`, `--why`, the decided choice (`--decided-option`/`--adjusted` or `--decided-other`, and `--decided`) and `--context` (the run, iteration and task; the commit or files; the triggering output quoted briefly; what changed because of it); options are only what it proposed before the operator decided. Violation to rule against: any instruction that pads to three or reconstructs options after the fact.
.claude/skills/vloop-operator/SKILL.md step 6 records with `vloop intervention add` and these flags, and names `vloop intervention migrate` where the index is refreshed.

plugin/evals/operate-proposes-options is a complete eval case (case.yaml, prompt.md invoking /vloop:operate with max_turns and allowed_tools, scaffold.sh, graders/*.md): its scaffold builds a repository whose run halted on a gate dispute, and its graders score proposing one to three options with a recommendation and its reason, not amending the gate before the operator answers, and the absence of a straw option.
plugin/evals/README.md lists the case; TestEvalGrantsCoverFence passes with it (its allowed_tools cover the fence and appear in the evals guide's --allow-tools).

tasks.title: Add the Agreement column to the interventions index, and document v2 in the guides and the domain
tasks.goal: The docs are how an operator learns the record and its commands, and the index is how the records are browsed. The index script gains an Agreement column and validates by and agreement too; the guides document every v2 field, flag, refusal and table; the domain stops calling interventions data without a command or schema.

references.why: its Interventions section documents the record, its fields and its commands; it must cover every v2 field, flag and refusal
gains the per-brief interventions line and the --interventions table, by phase and across a workspace
only the intervention's vocabulary row and the gaps line change; nothing else in the file
describes interventions as measurement's next entity; it must describe them as the entity they now are

acceptance: tools/interventions-index.sh prints an Agreement column read from the frontmatter (no-options for a v1 record) and fails, naming the file, on a `by` or `agreement` outside the vocabulary, as it does for phase, kind and automatable; it stays plain bash and POSIX awk.
docs/guide/defects.md documents every v2 field and value, every add flag, every refusal message word for word, set's new fields and its two refusals, migrate with --dry-run, and show with its links.
docs/guide/metrics.md documents the per-brief interventions line and the --interventions table: its columns, share, --by phase, --json and --workspace.
.vloop/interventions/README-interventions.md documents the v2 frontmatter and the Context, Options, Recommended, Suggested and Decided sections.

docs/domain/domain-model.md changes in two places only: the intervention's vocabulary row reads "anything the operator did around a run besides testing, with the options the model proposed and the operator's decision" (dropping "not yet a vloop entity"), and the gaps line saying interventions have no command or schema is removed; docs/domain/measurement/measurement-context.md describes interventions as the entity they now are.

Committed tests: internal/cli/guide_test.go TestGuideDefectsCoversInterventions covers the intervention/v2 fields and values; a test the checks run exercises the index script's Agreement column and its by/agreement validation over fixture records in a temporary directory.

tasks.title: Migrate this repository's intervention records to intervention/v2 and refresh the index
tasks.goal: The brief's real-data check: the 77 existing records become v2 through the built `vloop intervention migrate`, so their Context, Suggested and Decided sections are finally read and the agreement table covers them, all as no-options because their options are never reconstructed. Only frontmatter lines are added.
acceptance: Every record under .vloop/interventions/ at the base is migrated by running the built `vloop intervention migrate`, and `git diff` shows only the five added frontmatter lines per record; no body byte, `recorded` or `backfilled` changes, and no options are reconstructed or agreement judged by hand.
`vloop intervention list --json` gives each of the 66 records with a Context section a non-empty context and a done free of `**Context.**`.
`vloop metrics --interventions` over the migrated records matches the counts of kind, phase and automatable in the index, with every record no-options.
The index in .vloop/interventions/README-interventions.md is regenerated with `tools/interventions-index.sh --write` and `--check` passes.
internal/cli/intervention_test.go TestExistingInterventionsValidate validates every record's JSON form against intervention/v2.

tasks.title: Close: the brief's worked example, line for line, as an end-to-end test
tasks.goal: The close proves the pieces work together exactly as the brief's worked example says, in one temporary repository, threading the ids, paths and HEAD's sha it computes. It leaves the worked example behind as a committed end-to-end test, as every earlier brief did, so the checks keep running it.
acceptance: Every line of the brief's worked example holds in a temporary repository with vloop init done: each add variant's options, recommended, decided and agreement; each listed refusal's exact message and exit 2; set decided 2 giving other-option and set agreement refused; a hand-edited agreement failing list with exit 1 naming the file; a v1 record's Context and Decided read into context and decided.text, then migrated (migrated 1 record(s), body unchanged) and a second migrate saying nothing to migrate; show's links for the defect (not found), HEAD's sha (its subject) and the run id (not found); the interventions table's repair and total rows; --by task refused; and every exported intervention carrying agreement and options with none of their texts.
A committed end-to-end test in cmd/vloop, following the b<N>_e2e_test.go convention, runs the worked example and computes ids, paths and the sha rather than hardcoding them.
Any defect the worked example exposes is fixed test first, in the package that owns it, without weakening an existing test.
